questions.prompt: A Claude API key reaches its expiry date. What happens?

options.text: Requests keep working until someone renews it in the Console.
options.explanation: Claude does not renew keys. After expiry, requests fail.

options.text: Requests return 401 authentication_error, so create a new key.
options.explanation: Right. An expired key cannot be reactivated, so you create a replacement.

options.text: Requests return 429 until the first day of the next month.
options.explanation: That is the spend-cap behavior from chapter 1. An expired key gives an authentication error.

questions.prompt: An organization with OpenAI Zero Data Retention sends a Responses request with store: true. What happens?

options.text: The request fails with a 400 error, because store conflicts with ZDR.
options.explanation: The request does not fail. OpenAI changes how the parameter is treated.

options.text: The response is saved for 30 days, as the request asked.
options.explanation: That is the default without ZDR. With ZDR, the request's wish to store is ignored.

options.text: The store value is treated as false, even though it says true.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say that with ZDR, store is always treated as false.

questions.prompt: A Claude API key was created for a single workspace. Where does it work?

options.text: In every workspace of the organization, unless an admin turns it off.
options.explanation: A key scoped to one workspace cannot reach resources in other workspaces.

options.text: Only in that workspace, and requests can omit the workspace ID.
options.explanation: Right. Single-workspace keys only work there, so the anthropic-workspace-id header is not needed.

options.text: Only in the Default workspace, which every key can use.
options.explanation: A single-workspace key works only in the workspace it was made for.
